title: IIP for India’s textile manufacturing in Jul grows 3.9% to 135.5
summary:
The growth rate of India’s index of industrial production (IIP) for July was 6.7 per cent, quick official estimates show.
For the manufacturing sector, it was 7.3 per cent in July.  
The IIP for textile manufacturing in July grew by 3.9 per cent to 135.5, while the same for apparel manufacturing fell by 0.6 per cent to 95.9. 
The IIP for leather sector manufacturing in July grew by 0.8 per cent to 113.2.

title: Greece’s T&A imports reach $1.62 bn as apparel demand rises
summary:
Greece’s textile and apparel imports rose 1.79 per cent to $1.625 billion in January–June 2026, driven entirely by finished apparel.
Apparel imports increased 5.87 per cent to $1.265 billion, while textile imports fell 17.18 per cent and home textiles slipped 1.64 per cent.
Trousers and shorts led apparel imports at $286.771 million; fabric dominated textile imports with a 71.45 per cent share.

title: New Zealand exporters significantly benefiting from UAE FTA: Minister
summary:
Exporters in New Zealand are significantly benefiting from the free trade agreement with the UAE a year after it entered into force, according to the former’s Trade and Investment Minister Todd McClay. 
New Zealand’s goods exports to the UAE rose by 7 per cent to $1.4 billion in the first year of the FTA. 
Two-way goods trade exceeded $1.6 billion to July 2026.

title: Economic sentiment, employment expectations pick up in EU, euro area
summary:
The economic sentiment indicator rose in the EU by 1 point to 98.2 and in the euro area by 1.3 points to 98.4 in August 2026. 
The employment expectations indicator also picked up in August compared to July; it rose by 1.2 points to 99 in the EU, while for the euro area, it rose by 1.5 points to 98.9. 
Industry confidence in the EU rose in August by 0.4 point, while consumer confidence was broadly stable.

title: China's new economic growth drivers index up 12.5% in 2025
summary:
China's new economic growth drivers index rose by 12.5 per cent in 2025, with the transformation and upgrading index rising by 22.7 per cent  and contributing 34.1 per cent to overall index growth, and the innovation-driven index increasing by 12.9 per cent and contributing another 31.4 per cent. 
Both the latter indices jointly accounted for around two-thirds of the rise.

title: Import prices in Germany 6.8% higher YoY in Jul 2026: Destatis
summary:
Import prices in Germany were 6.8 per cent higher YoY and 0.2 per cent higher month on month (MoM) in July, official data show. 
Export prices were 4.2 per cent higher YoY in July—the largest YoY increase since February 2023; these were up by 0.4 per cent MoM in the month. Considerable YoY increases in import prices were recorded for mineral oil products, crude oil and natural gas.

title: Euro area M3 growth rises to 3.4% in July 2026
summary:
Euro area broad money M3 grew 3.4 per cent in July 2026, after 3.3 per cent in June, with the three-month average at 3.2 per cent.
Adjusted loans to non-financial corporations rose 4.4 per cent, signalling credit conditions relevant to suppliers and buyers.
Household loan growth edged to 3.1 per cent, while M1 eased to 3.1 per cent from 3.5 per cent.

title: ADB approves $400 mn plan to improve Central Asia trade links
summary:

For exporters, importers and sourcing teams, the focus is on lower transport and logistics costs across trade corridors.
The BUILD facility will finance road and rail border points, digital systems, inspection equipment and harmonised procedures.

title: Philippines growth forecast falls as exports offer support

Risks include energy prices, extreme weather and delayed public investment; policy is set to stay data-dependent on inflation.

title: France's industrial producer prices accelerate 4.3% in July
summary:

Home-market prices rebounded while foreign-market prices slowed monthly but rose faster annually, affecting export pricing signals.
Import prices of industrial products increased 0.8 per cent over a month and 6.6 per cent over a year.

title: Can solar energy ease Bangladesh RMG sector’s power woes?
summary:
Bangladesh garment factories could generate up to 1,768 MWp of rooftop solar using nearly 9.7 million square metres of roof space. 
It could meet around 40 per cent of large factories’ power demand, 38 per cent for small units and 33 per cent for medium units. 
Upfront costs, financing and technical barriers remain; BGMEA-Bidec fan trials saved 47 per cent to nearly 65 per cent electricity.

title: RMG sector faces stiffer competition, rising costs: Bangladesh Bank
summary:
Bangladesh’s RMG exports rose by 11 per cent YoY to $10.10 billion during Q4 FY26, the Bangladesh Bank’s quarterly review of the sector said. 
The central bank cautioned that the sector faces rising production costs and stiffer competition from rival exporting countries amid persistent global economic uncertainty and geopolitical tensions. 
The near-term outlook for the sector is moderately positive.

title: Australia’s babywear import prices rise; India retains second spot

India stayed second at $17.053 million, just $512,000 ahead of Bangladesh.
China, India and Bangladesh accounted for 92.48 per cent of imports.

title: Evolving Middle East crisis raising fresh risks for Indian exporters?
summary:
Iran-US tensions and Houthi attacks in the Red Sea are adding risks around the Strait of Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb for Indian businesses. 
Experts warn longer routes could lift freight costs, war-risk premiums and transit times while tightening vessel capacity. 
Readymade garment exporters to Europe may see pressure on prices, margins, delivery commitments and supply-chain certainty.
